To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the optimum topology of 1D PhCr plate unitcell with centric scattering inclusion is found to be a combination of a few different topologies, 2) the optimum topology is found to be dependent on the aspect ratio of unitcell and filling fraction, and 3) the optimum topology for centric unitcell is found to be symmetric.
The optimum topology of PhCr plate unitcell with one-dimensional periodicity is found to be a function of aspect ration, filling fraction, and prescribed symmetry.

the optimum topology of biaxial periodic plate with centric scattering inclusion is a combination of concentric rings of different thickness and width, with the outermost ring being the thickest and widest one.
In summary, our research is concerned with

optimum design of bimaterial PhCr plate structures to achieve maximum relative bandgap efficiency at a particular filling fraction and also to produce PhCr plates with gradient topology and enhanced bandgap efficiency.
the development of optimum topology and its application for the design of PhCr plate structures to obtain maximum relative bandgap widths of Lamb waves.
optimum design of PhCr plate unitcell and its application to produce finite PhCr plate structure with enhanced bandgap width and multiscale functionality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimum topology of PhCr plate unitcell with one-dimensional periodicity is a noncentric one and the bandgaps of such unitcells are more efficient than those of centric PhCr plates.

PhCr plate unitcell topology optimization is a powerful method for designing PhCr plate structures to achieve maximum bandgaps at desired frequency range, with high specific efficiency, or further with graded bandgaps and enhanced specific efficiency through multiscale functionality.
the proposed optimized topologies of PhCr plate unitcell with and without symmetry are capable of achieving higher bandgap width as compared to corresponding centric regular structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimum topologies obtained in this research could be used as a guideline for design of PhCr plates with maximum bandgap efficiency and/or multiscale functionality.
a few optimum PhCr plate topologies have been proposed to attain maximum bandgap efficiency for low order Lamb waves, and also the possibility for graded PhCr plate structure has been demonstrated.

the obtained optimum topological solutions can be used for the design of bimaterial PhCr plate structures to attain maximum bandgap width of particular low order Lamb waves at specific filling fraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimum topology of PhCr plate unitcell is highly dependent on aspect ratio, prescribed symmetry and filling fraction of constituents.

by optimizing the topology of PhCr plates, one can achieve a significant improvement in the bandgap width and efficiency, and also the possibility of producing graded PhCr plate structure for enhanced performance.
the bandgap of PhCr plates can be enhanced by optimized topology of the unitcell, which can be achieved by a multiobjective GA in conjunction with FEM.
